speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent, and I will be conducting your examination today. To begin, can you describe the nature of your fatigue and how long you have been experiencing this severe itching?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any dark urine, pale stools, or jaundice? I would also like to know if you have experienced any recent weight loss or abdominal pain.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis and current signs of cholestasis, I suspect a biliary issue. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel, IgG4_levels, MRCP.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver_Function_Panel: Bilirubin_Total 1.5 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Direct 0.9 mg/dL, Alkaline_Phosphatase 460 U/L, AST 75 U/L, ALT 78 U/L. IgG4_levels: NORMAL READINGS. MRCP: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal MRCP rules out large duct obstruction, and normal IgG4 makes autoimmune pancreatitis unlikely, but the cholestatic pattern with ulcerative colitis strongly suggests Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. I need to evaluate for liver inflammation and fibrosis to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Biopsy, Antimitochondrial_Antibody

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver_Biopsy: Findings consistent with Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (onion-skin fibrosis). Antimitochondrial_Antibody: Negative

speaker: Doctor
text: The liver biopsy showing onion-skin fibrosis confirms the diagnosis of Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis, especially given your history of ulcerative colitis and cholestatic liver enzymes. DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
